speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; this constellation of symptoms is concerning for a serious underlying condition. To begin our investigation, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits, such as constipation, diarrhea, or a change in stool caliber?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The "drenching night sweats" and 12-pound weight loss are significant "B symptoms" that strongly suggest lymphoma or another malignancy. To evaluate the abdominal pain and the lymph nodes more specifically, can you tell me if you have noticed any lumps under your skin in other areas, or any skin rashes?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient's report confirms worsening fatigue, pain, night sweats, and weight loss but provides no mention of skin rashes or other palpable lumps. With your B symptoms and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, I need to determine the origin of the lymph nodes; do you notice any swelling in your neck or armpits, and has your appetite changed recently?

REQUEST TEST: Lactate_Dehydrogenase (LDH)
REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate (ESR)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lactate_Dehydrogenase: Elevated; Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The elevated LDH combined with your B symptoms and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is highly concerning for a lymphoproliferative disorder, likely lymphoma, despite the normal ESR. To help localize the disease, specifically to evaluate for involvement of the abdomen and to look for any skin or subcutaneous lesions, I need you to describe the nature of your abdominal pain and allow me to examine your abdomen and skin.

REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis, Dermoscopy

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The sensation of abdominal fullness and tighter clothes suggests an expanding mass, possibly in the liver or retroperitoneum. Have you noticed any jaundice, changes in your urine color, or back pain?

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Test
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Palpation

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Test: NORMAL READINGS; Abdominal_Palpation: Splenomegaly detected, without rebound tenderness; Inspection: Slight abdominal distension; Percussion: Dullness noted over the left lower quadrant

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, elevated LDH, and B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) is highly suspicious for a systemic lymphoproliferative disorder, likely Hodgkin or Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma.

Given the splenomegaly and abdominal fullness, do you have any history of alcohol use that might cause liver issues, or have you experienced easy bruising or bleeding gums?

REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Blood_Smear
REQUEST TEST: Flow_Cytometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Peripheral_Blood_Smear: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20; Flow_Cytometry: Positive for B-cell markers consistent with CD20+ population

speaker: Doctor
text:
The peripheral blood smear showing proliferating lymphocytes and the flow cytometry confirming a CD20+ B-cell population strongly suggest a B-cell lymphoma. Given your history of B symptoms, splenomegaly, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, what is the approximate size of your supraclavicular node, and have you noticed any pruritus (itching), particularly at night?

REQUEST TEST: Bone_Marrow_Biopsy
REQUEST TEST: PET_CTA

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bone_Marrow_Biopsy: Findings consistent with lymphoma infiltration; PET_CTA: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes; increased metabolic activity in spleen and supraclavicular region

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL)

The combination of B symptoms, massive lymphadenopathy on PET/CT, splenomegaly, and flow cytometry confirming a CD20+ B-cell population is diagnostic for aggressive B-cell lymphoma.
